claims.claim: Kiefer and Ryzhikov use the all-word k-image-bounded model and incompleteness means existence of a mortal word.
Kiefer and Ryzhikov give M_k(n)<=n^(k+1) and ask whether the bound is tight.
For every k>=2 and every n>=2k+2A_k k!, the binary strongly connected construction has mortality at least k! n^(k+1)/(2A_k)^(k+1), hence M_k(n)=Theta_k(n^(k+1)).
The unrestricted subset bound is 2^n-1, ruling out a jointly tight n^(k+1) estimate for growing k.
The quadratic order at k=1 is known; Ryzhikov Section 4 recalls sharp unrestricted-alphabet n(n+1)/2 and attributes it to Rystsov.
Ryzhikov Section 4 gives a binary deterministic queue and physical delay path; the queue action here agrees up to indexing.
Ryzhikov unrestricted NFA exponential lower bounds do not impose the global k-image promise.
Ananichev Section 2 Lemma 2.1 reproduces Vorel appended-tail lemma: under almost-permutation and divisibility conditions, h extra states add rh to reset threshold.
The shared k-clock packet has period L=lcm(ell_i) using sum ell_i clock states; coprime lengths permit fixed-k order n^k.
Every singleton image is empty, singleton or a single packet; least global image bound is exactly k and the graph is strongly connected.
After the first b, the global image is P union S and V=m+1.
Every b-boundary has form T union E_eta and V_old-V_new=eta-epsilon; each unit drop requires L dividing t+1.
Every mortal word costs at least 1+(m+1)L.
An explicit mortal word has length at most 1+(m+1)L+m^2, without a condition on gcd(m,L).
The displayed parameter choice gives exactly n states, m>=M>=n/(2A), pairwise-coprime ell_i and L>=k! M^k for every n>=N_k.
Successive killing of original rows gives at most nD<=n^(k+1) letters.
The b^(2r) relation has k^r paths from p_0 to itself; endpoints merge.
A separately implemented verifier covered 22 finite instances, including repeated and noncoprime clock lengths.
